notes.text: Taken away — Abolished, and put an end to the judgments thy sins brought upon thee. Thine enemy - The Babylonian. Is in the midst - He is returned to redeem and govern thee. Any more - While thy carriage is as becomes my presence with thee, thou shalt neither fear, nor feel the like evils.
Sorrowful — That mourn their distance from the solemn worship of God. Who are of thee - Thy children. Reproach - The taunts of their enemies.
Undo — I will break their power and dissolve their kingdom. That halteth - Who is in trouble and ready to fall. Driven out - Into remote countries.
A praise — So the universal church of the first-born will be, in the great day. And then the Israel of God be made a name and a praise to all eternity.
God — My salvation hath not been brought to pass by man, but by the almighty power of God.

With joy — Your thirsty souls shall be filled with Divine graces and comforts, which you may draw from God, in the use of gospel-ordinances. God's armies, ver. 1-5. The destruction of Babylon by the Persians and Medes, their great distress, anguish, and utter desolation, ver. 6-22.

glossa.text: *Out of the fountains of the Saviour.* ((ID.)) Whence: *Bless ye the Lord from the fountains of Israel,* etc., *as far as* that the prophecy may agree with the Gospel.

notes.text: Let your gentleness — Yieldingness, sweetness of temper, the result of joy in the Lord. Be known - By your whole behaviour. To all men - Good and bad, gentle and froward. Those of the roughest tempers are good natured to some, from natural sympathy and various motives; a Christian, to all. The Lord - The judge, the rewarder, the avenger. Is at hand - Standeth at the door.

Be anxiously careful for nothing — If men are not gentle towards you, yet neither on this, nor any other account, be careful, but pray. Carefulness and prayer cannot stand together. In every thing - Great and small. Let your requests be made known - They who by a preposterous shame or distrustful modesty, cover, stifle, or keep in their desires, as if they were either too small or too great, must be racked with care; from which they are entirely delivered, who pour them out with a free and filial confidence. To God - It is not always proper to disclose them to men. By supplication - Which is the enlarging upon and pressing our petition. With thanksgiving - The surest mark of a soul free from care, and of prayer joined with true resignation. This is always followed by peace. Peace and thanksgiving are both coupled together, Colossians iii, 15.

And the peace of God — That calm, heavenly repose, that tranquility of spirit, which God only can give. Which surpasseth all understanding - Which none can comprehend, save he that receiveth it. Shall keep - Shall guard, as a garrison does a city. Your hearts - Your affections. Your minds - Your understandings, and all the various workings of them; through the Spirit and power of Christ Jesus, in the knowledge and love of God. Without a guard set on these likewise, the purity and vigour of our affections cannot long be preserved.

glossa.text: *Rejoice,* etc. Being gladdened over their faith and their works, the Apostle, that they may be the more eager, desires that they, advancing in this zeal, should rejoice in the Lord, and he repeats it, that he may show that he truly rejoices in them.

*Moderation.* That is, right measure, so that all joy may be in the Lord, and that others may learn this through you. Or, *let moderation be known to all,* faithful and unbelieving, that they may imitate it, lest they be able to reprehend. *The Lord is nigh,* that is, ready to give whatsoever is needful in spiritual or in temporal things. Be solicitous and fearful about nothing. But your petitions concerning those things which you wish to obtain.

*But in every prayer.* Prayer and supplication are made in common for oneself or for others, concerning whatsoever things, but petition is made concerning things necessary by name. *Let them be made known.* This making known comes about by assiduity, and by watchfulness of prayer. Then at last peace keeps the hearts in Christ. He says this for this reason, because he who has peace with God does not fear an adverse mind. *With God.* Or to the angels, who offer them to God. Whence: When you were praying, I offered your prayer before God. Or, let them be made known for us with God through endurance, not with men through boasting.

*And the peace of God,* that is, God, who is the highest peace, which cannot even be thought, and therefore outside him there is need of nothing. *It surpasseth all understanding.* Ours, not that of those who always behold the face of the Father. Or, the peace whereby God himself is at peace *surmounts all understanding:* except his own, because neither can we know it thus, nor can any angels.

notes.text: Say not within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father — That is, trust not in your being members of the visible Church, or in any external privileges whatsoever: for God now requires a change of heart; and that without delay.

He answereth — It is not properly John, but the Holy Ghost, who teaches us in the following answers, how to come ourselves, and how to instruct other penitent sinners to come to Christ, that he may give them rest. The sum of all this is, Cease to do evil, learn to do well. These are the fruits worthy of repentance.

glossa.text: *Who hath shewed,* etc.? ((AMBR.)) Who hath shewed, in the prudence poured in by the mercy of God, etc.? *as far as* which he prophesies is to be transferred to the Gentiles.
*For I say to you. ((ID.))* They who, having lost the sense of reason, etc., *as far as* they are filled with fruits, they are clothed with leaves.
*He that hath two. (BEDA)*. The tunic is more necessary of itself than the cloak, etc., *as far as* but let him share what he has with the poor man.
*The publicans. ((ID.))* They who exact the public tolls, etc., *as far as* they might at length attain to sharing their own goods with their neighbours.
*And while they were supposing. ((ID.))* Not only were they thinking, etc., *as far as* they do not believe that he came through a virgin.

*But there shall come.* Therefore I baptize with water, because he comes who will baptize with the Spirit, and it is fitting that a way be prepared for him.

*Whose I am not worthy. ((BEDA.))* I am not worthy to search out the mystery of the incarnation, etc., *as far as* the evangelical preaching, with which the apostles are shod.

Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
echoes.note: 'The Lord is at hand' (ho kyrios engys) most closely matches 'The LORD is near to all who call on him' (engys kyrios), grounding Paul's nearness claim and its link to prayer in v.6. High lexical volume on engys, coherence with the prayer/petition context, and availability in the LXX Psalter make this the strongest source for the phrase.

echoes.text: Be glad in Yahweh, and rejoice, you righteous! Shout for joy, all you who are upright in heart!
echoes.note: 'Rejoice in the LORD always' echoes the recurrent Psalter imperative 'Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, you righteous' (32:11; cf. 33:1; 97:12). Recurrence is strong across the Psalter and coherence with Paul's joy theme is high; volume is moderate because Paul universalizes 'always' beyond any single psalm.

echoes.text: Be glad in Yahweh, you righteous people! Give thanks to his holy Name.
echoes.note: 'Rejoice in the LORD, O you righteous' supplies the same divine-object joy imperative that Paul doubles for emphasis. The Psalter's habitual call to rejoice in the LORD is available and coherent, though the volume of any single verse is moderate given the formula's diffusion.

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is near to the brokenhearted' reinforces the 'Lord is near' motif with the same engys idiom, and Psalm 34 broadly underwrites Paul's confidence in deliverance. Recurrence of the nearness formula with Psalm 145 strengthens coherence, though volume per verse is moderate.

echoes.text: Be silent at the presence of the Lord Yahweh, for the day of Yahweh is at hand. For Yahweh has prepared a sacrifice. He has consecrated his guests.
echoes.note: 'The day of the LORD is at hand/near' supplies the eschatological-imminence sense of 'The Lord is at hand,' if Paul means the Lord's coming rather than his presence. Availability in the prophetic day-of-the-Lord tradition and coherence with Philippians' Parousia hope (3:20) support this, though it competes with the Psalter nearness reading.

echoes.text: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
echoes.note: 'You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you' parallels Paul's 'peace of God which surpasses all understanding will guard your hearts,' linking divine peace, the mind, and protective keeping. Coherence is strong on the guarding-peace-of-the-mind motif; volume is moderate because Paul does not quote the phrasing verbatim.

echoes.text: Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
echoes.note: 'Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you' parallels Paul's remedy for anxiety: hand your requests to God in prayer rather than carry them. Coherence with the anti-anxiety-through-petition logic is strong; volume is moderate since Paul shares the idea, not the wording.

echoes.text: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.
echoes.note: 'In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for you alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety' offers the OT pairing of divine peace with security from anxiety that underlies 'do not be anxious... and the peace of God will guard you.' Volume is low and the link thematic, so this is a contributing echo.

echoes.text: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
echoes.note: 'Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad' supplies a wisdom backdrop for Paul's 'in nothing be anxious.' Volume and verbal overlap are slight, but the heart-anxiety theme is available in the sapiential tradition, making this a faint echo.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: They hatch adders’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web: he who eats of their eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper.
echoes.note: "Offspring of vipers" draws on the prophetic image of the wicked hatching adders' eggs (Isaiah 59:5), where viper-brood imagery signals deadly, deceitful evildoers under judgment. Coherence with John's judgment oracle is strong; the serpent-progeny metaphor is distinctly prophetic.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, you who follow after righteousness, you who seek Yahweh: look to the rock you were cut from, and to the hold of the pit you were dug from. Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.
echoes.note: "God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones" plays on Isaiah 51:1-2, which calls Israel to "look to the rock from which you were hewn ... to Abraham your father," the rock-Abraham-descendants nexus John inverts. The shared Abraham-from-stone logic gives this real Volume; possible Hebrew wordplay (banim/abanim, children/stones) strengthens the link.

echoes.text: Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low. He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
echoes.note: "The axe lies at the root of the trees" and trees cut down echoes Isaiah 10:33-34, where the LORD lops the boughs and hews down the forest of the arrogant in judgment. The arboreal-judgment imagery and verb of cutting give solid Coherence with John's eschatological warning.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: Trees that bear no good fruit being "cut down and thrown into the fire" coheres with Malachi 4:1 (3:19 MT), where the day comes burning like an oven, leaving the wicked neither root nor branch. The root/branch and burning-judgment vocabulary reinforce the eschatological-fire theme John develops in v.17.

echoes.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
echoes.note: The "offspring of vipers" may evoke the serpent's seed of Genesis 3, casting the unrepentant as children of the primeval serpent in opposition to God. Faint and figural; marked low since the immediate force is prophetic invective rather than a Genesis citation.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, Son of man, what is the vine tree more than any tree, the vine-branch which is among the trees of the forest? Will wood be taken of it to make anything? Will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel on it? Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire has devoured both its ends, and its midst is burned: is it profitable for any work? Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less, when the fire has […]
echoes.note: Ezekiel's parable of the useless vine fit only for the fire parallels the unfruitful tree consigned to burning. A reinforcing instance of the prophetic fruitless-wood-to-fire judgment topos; low and contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh called your name, A green olive tree, beautiful with goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he has kindled fire on it, and its branches are broken. For Yahweh of Armies, who planted you, has pronounced evil against you, because of the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have worked for themselves in provoking me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
echoes.note: Jeremiah likens Israel to a once-green tree the LORD sets on fire and whose branches are broken for evil done, matching John's unfruitful-tree-cast-into-fire image. Faint reinforcing echo within the prophetic tree-judgment field; low.

echoes.text: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.
echoes.note: The fruit-bearing-tree-versus-judgment contrast inverts Psalm 1's tree that yields fruit in season; John warns that fruitlessness ends in fire. Thematic and faint; the Volume is low and the link is contested.

echoes.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
echoes.note: John's practical ethics of justice and mercy (share clothing/food, no extortion, no false accusation) embody Micah 6:8's demand to do justice and love mercy as the true fruit of repentance. The prophetic reduction of repentance to concrete social righteousness gives strong Coherence with John's program.

echoes.text: “Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the bands of the yoke, and to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?
echoes.note: "He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none ... he who has food" closely matches Isaiah 58:7's true fast: share bread with the hungry and cover the naked. The verbal pairing of clothing and food for the destitute gives this real Volume as the prophetic template for John's instruction.

echoes.text: But if a man is just, and does that which is lawful and right, and has not eaten on the mountains, neither has lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, neither has defiled his neighbor’s wife, neither has come near to a woman in her impurity, and has not wronged any, but has restored to the debtor his pledge, has taken nothing by robbery, has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment; he who has not lent on […]
echoes.note: Ezekiel 18's portrait of the righteous man (gives bread to the hungry, covers the naked, takes no usury/extortion, returns the pledge) directly parallels John's checklist of repentant conduct. The catalog of just deeds as the mark of the one who lives gives strong Coherence with John's "fruits worthy of repentance."

echoes.text: “‘You shall not steal. “‘You shall not lie. “‘You shall not deceive one another. “‘You shall not swear by my name falsely, and profane the name of your God. I am Yahweh. “‘You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him. “‘The wages of a hired servant shall not remain with you all night until the morning.
echoes.note: John's charges to soldiers and tax collectors not to extort, defraud, or accuse falsely echo the Holiness Code's prohibitions of robbery, fraud, and oppression of the wage-laborer (Lev 19:11-13). A reinforcing legal substratum for John's ethic; low and contested.

echoes.text: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail, or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her have I guided from my mother’s womb); if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering; if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
echoes.note: Job's oath of innocence (he did not withhold bread from the poor or let any perish for lack of clothing) parallels John's clothing-and-food charity. Part of the wider OT righteousness-as-mercy field; faint and low.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to Yahweh offerings in righteousness.
echoes.note: The Coming One who baptizes "with the Holy Spirit and fire" and refines/purges directly answers Malachi 3:2-3, where the messenger of the covenant is like a refiner's fire purifying the sons of Levi. The pairing of fire with purgative judgment-and-cleansing gives high Coherence with John's contrast between the mightier one and himself.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: The winnowing fork separating wheat from chaff to be burned with unquenchable fire mirrors Malachi 4:1 (3:19 MT), where the day burns like a furnace and the wicked are stubble. The threshing-floor/chaff-versus-grain judgment and the inextinguishable fire give this strong Volume.

echoes.text: “They shall go out, and look on the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”
echoes.note: "Unquenchable fire" (pyr asbeston) echoes Isaiah 66:24, where the fire upon the rebels' corpses is not quenched, the OT locus for everlasting judgment-fire. The precise eschatological-fire vocabulary gives this real Volume within John's threshing-floor oracle.

echoes.text: I have winnowed them with a fan in the gates of the land; I have bereaved them of children, I have destroyed my people; they didn’t return from their ways.
echoes.note: "I have winnowed them with a fan in the gates of the land" (Jeremiah 15:7) supplies the divine-winnowing image of separating people for judgment that underlies John's fan and threshing floor. The agricultural-judgment metaphor (winnow/scatter the unfaithful) gives solid Coherence.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The promise that the Coming One "will baptize you in the Holy Spirit" resonates with Joel's outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh, a text Luke develops at Pentecost. Faint here, foreshadowing the Lukan Spirit theme; low and contested as the immediate image is refining fire.

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: Spirit-baptism that purifies recalls Ezekiel 36:25-27, where God sprinkles clean water and puts a new Spirit within his people. A reinforcing prophetic Spirit-and-cleansing background for the contrast between water and Spirit baptism; low.

echoes.text: Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff. You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahweh. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
echoes.note: Isaiah 41:15-16 makes Israel a threshing sledge that winnows mountains so the wind carries them off, another winnowing-judgment image feeding John's fan and chaff. Faint reinforcing echo within the OT threshing-floor field; low and contested.

lines: Sing aloud; do not fear.
The Lord our God is in our midst.
Shout for joy; the Lord has taken away the judgment against you.
The Lord our God is in our midst.
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice.
Come, let us worship with joy. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Can you hear it? Under the gray of these short days, a song is starting up.
Joy is welling up like water.
The Lord has turned away your shame and gathered the ones who grieved.
Joy is welling up like water.
With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
Joy is welling up like water.
So do not be anxious; the Lord is near, and near is no small thing.
Joy is welling up like water. Rejoice!
